Press Release:


Estina Dairy Farm 3
For years, the Estina Dairy farm project, which was intended for the benefit of local Free State farmers, has been at the centre of state capture. Now as investigations into the controversial project continue, the Hawks have made eight major arrests and seized property from some of the accused. South Africa’s elite crime fighting unit insists that there are still more suspects to apprehend. Carte Blanche asks: Is the net finally closing in on the Gupta empire?


Script:


GUPTA DAIRY FARM 2

V/O: Earlier this year Carte Blanche brought you a follow-up to our 2014 expose of the Vrede Dairy Farm scam. This saw the Guptas and their associates plundering State coffers, with the help of individuals in the Free State Department of Agriculture.

This R342 million project had promised 600 jobs, and a livelihood for 100 emerging farmers. But only R2 million actually went to the farm. The cows were diseased, and the locals remained unemployed.

In January the Asset Forfeiture Unit obtained a preservation order from the Bloemfontein High Court, allowing them to freeze R220 million that had been stolen from the project, and distributed to various Gupta-linked entities and associates. R10 million went to Atul Gupta himself.

Only two weeks later, there was a seismic shift in the political landscape. With the end of the Zuma era, the Hawks swooped on the Gupta compound, brandishing warrants of arrest.

Devi link: The last time we were here, things were very different: the Guptas were in the house, Jacob Zuma was in the House, and it seemed to be business as usual in Saxonwold. But on Valentine's Day everything changed. The Hawks raided the Gupta compound, Jacob Zuma resigned as President, and the next day 8 accused stood in the dock of Bloemfontein Court.

V/O: Understandably security was tight and most media were not allowed in. But in the first case of State Capture to be prosecuted in a court of law, the charge sheet revealed that a total of R250 million was paid to Estina.

Accused Number 1 is Peter Thabethe, HOD of Free State Agriculture. He is charged with Fraud, Theft, Conspiracy to Commit Fraud or Theft, and Contravening the Public Finance Management Act.

Accused Number 2 is Seipati Dlamini, the former Chief Financial Officer for Free State Agriculture. She faces charges of Fraud, Theft, and Conspiracy to Commit Fraud or Theft, as does her colleague in the Department, Dr TJ Masiteng



Accused Number 4 is Estina. The company was placed in voluntary liquidation last year, but is now charged with Contravening the Prevention of Organized Crime Act.

Estina's former Director, Kamal Vasram, got 10% of the spoils, but for R25 million he is also facing criminal charges.

Oakbay Investments, the Gupta Company that received R24.5 million from Estina, is Accused Number 6, and Oakbay Director Ashu Chawla is also accused of contravening the Prevention of Organized Crime Act.

Facing the same charges are two former Oakbay Directors, Nazeem Howa, and Gupta family member, Varun Gupta.

Ronica Ragavan, is the CEO of Oakbay and Director of Tegeta Resources and Aero/haven Trading.

Aerohaven, which received R21million from Estina, is Accused Number 11.

Magda: They were key lieutenants and key enablers of the Gupta empire, and key participants in state capture project. So, if you look at GuptaLeaks, they were all over Gupta Leaks.

V/O: Magda Wierzycka (Veer-zitjz-ka) is an asset manager who has become an anti-corruption crusader.

Magda: That dairy project was the bit that exposed them for what they are; for their lack of humanity, for the thieves that were willing to rob the poorest of the poor. Now when you are stealing from Eskom through a rigged tender, when you're stealing from Transnet through a locomotive deal, you can maybe persuade yourself that it's a victimless crime, it's just money. But here, the beginnings of your thievery actually involve real people, so that means you are not just a white-collar criminal, it actually means you're a flipping psychopath who is willing to rob and do absolutely anything, and you've got no conscience.

V/O: Conspicuously absent from this collection of cloaked suspects, are the Gupta brothers themselves - Ajay, Atul and Rajesh. According to authorities, they are not suspects in the case at this stage.

Brig: Well the country can expect more arrests. It is just a matter of us having to finalise the processes that we have already undertaken.

V/O: Brigadier Hangwani Moo/laud/zi is spokesperson for the Hawks, and he's playing his cards close to his chest.

Brigadier: I can confirm that there are warrants of arrest that are active. The names thereof I cannot mention. The only name that we did mention was for Mr Ajay Gupta. Mr Ajay Gupta is wanted for unrelated case, it is not directed to Estina.

V/O: But Ajay Gupta was seen leaving the country on the 6th of February, much to the frustration of the Hawks.

Brigadier: We've been ready, ready to execute these warrants of arrests for a very long time. Let's not be shy about it. We've been ready. The investigation was completed in November.

Link: By the time the NPA issued the arrest warrants and the Hawks swooped on Saxonwold, the Gupta brothers were long gone. It's not clear if they were tipped off or if they decided to bolt after the Asset Forfeiture Unit came after them in January.

V/O: But Ajay is a fugitive on the run, and there's a million rand reward for information on their whereabouts. It is Magda herself who has contributed R900 000 to the reward.

Magda: Sometimes you need a trigger to incentivize good behavior. Sometimes you need something that makes you aware of the magnitude of what has happened, to pay a little bit more attention, and do the right thing.

V/O: The Guptas could be anywhere - from their Clifftop Safari Lodge in Limpopo, to their Emirates Hills mansion in Dubai, or one of their homes in India. When Atul Gupta challenged the Preservation Order for the R10 million he received from Estina, he signed his affidavit in Dubai.

Magda: I believe they are in India. It's a very large country to hide in. Dubai is a gilded cage. It's very difficult to either hide in Dubai or do anything in Dubai. India is almost a continent, and hence I believe - and also through information I've received - they're in India.

Devi: Do you know where the Gupta brothers are?

Brig: Well, I have been informed by the team they are aware where they are, and we are also working with other stakeholders giving us information.

Link: Obviously the Guptas are not going to return to South Africa of their own volition anytime soon. The next logical step to apprehend a fugitive is extradition, but that's not a simple process.

Ottillia: In an extradition request, you have to itemize everything that the person is being charged with; you also have to say in that letter that all of these charges are also offences in the country you are requesting it in. It is on that basis that the person then gets extradited to South Africa.

V/O: Ottilia Anna Maun/ga/nidze is an international criminal law expert with the Institute for Security Studies.

Devi: So it's not just the Estina Dairy farm case, there are allegations relating to Eskom, PRASA, Denel?

Ottilia: Remember there's also a Commission of Enquiry into Sate Capture, for which we're still waiting on additional information, so it might be prudent to wait a little bit.

V/O: While South Africa has an extradition treaty with India, we don't have one with the United Arab Emirates.

Ottilia: What exists at the moment is an international protocol dealing with organised crime, of which corruption is also included. As far as I know, both South Africa and the UAE are signatories.

V/O: But how will we get our money back? According to the charge sheet, Estina transferred R169 million to the Gupta-owned Gateway company in Dubai. Another R104 million went to an account at the Bank of Baroda. It's been reported that the Guptas peddled R4.5bn through the Johannesburg branch in the last decade. The Bank of Baroda is leaving South Africa at the end of the month, but has agreed to provide all the Gupta's banking records.

Magda: I know that FBI is looking at all the transactions where the money touched the US dollar, because that affects them, that affects American banks. In the UK, the FCA is following HSBC, and they've got the HSBC bank records so again you've just got to follow the bank transaction. You can split the money and split the money, but eventually with sufficient due diligence you can trace the final destination of the money.

V/O: But what about the man who admits the Vrede Dairy Farm project was his brainchild - the former MEC of Agriculture in the Free State, Mosebenzi Zwane?

Zwane: The idea behind the Vrede Dairy came with me, so that everybody knows. I initiated it. The project was not approved by me, it was approved by the whole Free State legislature, that includes EFF. It is on record, the honorable member was not there - go and check your records in the Free State.

EFF: Chairperson, this is out of order. This project was initiated in 2012. The EFF came in to form part of elections in 2014. This man is, this man is mad.

V/O: Since last week, Mosebenzi Zwane, is no longer the Minister of Mineral Resources.

Anton: The fact that it was his conceptual idea is mentioned in the charge sheet, however he's not charged.

V/O: Anton van Dalsen is the legal counsellor for the Helen Suzman Foundation. They're pursuing a civil case against 75 people mentioned in the GuptaLeaks, including Zwane.

Anton: It would be for the State to prove that he knew it was an illegal process, that he knew that State money was being used in a fraudulent manner, and the State would have to prove that.




V/O: Zwane might be out of a job, but his former colleague, Peter Thabethe is still at work in the Department. We asked him for comment, but all our requests were ignored. However, when we filmed his house in this modest Bloemfontein suburb, he suddenly gave us his full attention.

Peter: Why are you intruding into my private space?

Kate: We understand you are, I think you're Accused Number One in the Vrede Dairy case?

Sine: No you can't do that.

Peter: No, but you are doing it. What do you mean you can't do that?

Kate: Now you're in my private space.

Peter: No, but you have entered my private space.

Peter: Sharp. I'm reporting it right now.

Kate: Ok.

V/O: Peter Thabethe and his co-accused are out on bail and will appear in Court in Bloemfontein again on the 17th of August.
